# opwan_firewall (Resource)

The inbound firewall of one of the account's addresses. Rules are checked in order and the first match wins. TCP port 25 is always blocked, whatever the rules say. Destroying this resource restores the firewall of a new address: allow everything, no rules.

## Example Usage

```terraform
data "opwan_account" "this" {}

resource "opwan_firewall" "web" {
  ip             = data.opwan_account.this.addresses[0].ip
  default_action = "deny"

  rules = [
    { action = "allow", protocol = "tcp", ports = "80, 443" },
    { action = "allow", protocol = "udp", ports = "51000-51100", source = "203.0.113.0/24" },
    { action = "allow", protocol = "icmp" },
  ]
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `default_action` (String) What happens to inbound traffic no rule matches: `allow` or `deny`.
- `ip` (String) One of the account's addresses (dotted IPv4).

### Optional

- `rules` (Attributes List) The rules, checked in order, first match wins. At most 64. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--rules))

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) The address, same as `ip`.

<a id="nestedatt--rules"></a>
### Nested Schema for `rules`

Required:

- `action` (String) `allow` or `deny`.
- `protocol` (String) `tcp`, `udp`, `icmp` or `any`.

Optional:

- `ports` (String) Ports and ranges separated by commas (`"80, 443, 8000-8100"`, at most 32), `tcp` and `udp` only. Unset for every port. A TCP rule can't include port 25: split ranges around it (`"1-24, 26-1024"`).
- `source` (String) An IPv4 address or CIDR the traffic must come from. Unset for anywhere.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Import by address.
terraform import opwan_firewall.web 72.244.89.10
```
